scope_note: Release 'Issued by the: Office of the Legislative Assembly', with the in-text dateline '17 July 2012', on the government portal (raw Internet Archive capture of 11 April 2013).

rows.text: The Office of the Legislative Assembly's release states: '17 July 2012. His Majesty King Tupou VI under Clause 61(2) (c) of the Constitution has revoked Lord Lasike's appointment as the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Tonga effective immediately', and that this 'was conveyed in a letter to Havea Hikule'o Tu'uhetoka on the 17th of July 2012'.
rows.locator: Article body, first and second text paragraphs
rows.uncertainty: The revocation instrument itself was not seen and its own signature date is not printed; the release dates the letter conveying it to 17 July 2012 and says the revocation took effect immediately. The addressee is printed as Havea Hikule'o Tu'uhetoka; identity rests on the release naming Lord Lasike, not on matching spellings.

rows.text: The release states that the letter advised him of the consequence of his conviction on 9 July 2012 by the Supreme Court of an offence under section 4(2)(b) of the Arms and Ammunition Act, punishable by imprisonment for a maximum of 5 years (the sentence is unfinished as printed); in a separate paragraph, in the release's own voice, it states that 'Under Clause 23 of the Constitution the decision was effective from the date of his conviction and he is no longer an elected representative to the Legislative Assembly of Tonga'.
rows.locator: Article body, second and third text paragraphs
rows.uncertainty: Concerns his seat as an elected nobles' representative, the ground for revocation under clause 61(2)(c); it is not read as the end of the Speakership, which the release says was revoked effective immediately on 17 July. 'The decision was effective from the date of his conviction' is kept as printed.
